# Instructions for agents

<!-- generated by the platform at Connect -->
Generated from the Project's gate and stack packs when it was connected; the Knowledge Run may extend it. Rules marked *enforced* are checked by the platform and fail the step if broken.

## Stack and dependencies
- `backend` (backend): Python with pytest.
- `frontend` (frontend): TypeScript or JavaScript on Node, with Jest or Vitest, and Playwright end to end.
- Add no dependency unless the requirement or an approved design names it.

Component `backend` (folder `backend`): Python. `$python` is the Project's interpreter; use it for every Python command (`$python -m pytest`), never a
bare `python` or `pip`. To make the project importable (tests that start mypy or the package in a subprocess),
install it in editable mode (`$python -m pip install -e .`): each Run and snapshot has its own environment, so it
points at that Run's own worktree. Never a non-editable install (`pip install .`): checks would test a copy.
Install the tool versions the repo pins (its lock files, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, CI workflow, `==` pins), not
the latest: tests that compare a tool's output (mypy, black) fail on a newer one. Never leave a test out of a test
command (`--deselect`, `-k`, `--ignore`): a test failing on the default branch stays in, and its report makes it a
known failure the gate review accepts. Quote arguments with double quotes (`"mypy==1.9.0"`, `".[tests]"`): on
Windows a command runs in cmd.exe, which keeps single quotes, and on CI in bash. Tests are pytest functions named `test_*` in `tests/`. The platform's security
check runs `$python -m ruff`, so the install commands must install ruff.

Component `frontend` (folder `frontend`): Node with TypeScript. Commands run in a POSIX shell (bash), on this machine as on CI. Install from the lock file
with its own package manager: `npm ci` for `package-lock.json`, `bun ci` for `bun.lock`, `pnpm install
--frozen-lockfile` for `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn install --immutable` for `yarn.lock`; never an install that
rewrites the lock file. A test is an `it(...)`/`test(...)` in a `*.test.ts` or `*.spec.ts` file; never leave
`.only` or `.skip` in one. Don't run `npx` or `bunx` for a package that isn't already a dependency.

## Layout
- Component `backend`: folder `backend`, tests in `tests/*`, `test_*.py`, `*_test.py`
- Component `frontend`: folder `frontend`, tests in `*.test.ts`, `*.test.tsx`, `*.spec.ts`, `*.spec.tsx`, `*.test.js`, `*.spec.js`, `__tests__/*`, `*/__tests__/*`
- The code map (`docs/agents/CODEBASE_MAP.md`) comes with the Project's Knowledge Run; until then, read the build files and the folders your change touches before changing them.

## Coding conventions
- Follow the conventions of the code around your change: naming, error handling, logging and public API style. The reviewers check them.

## Testing
- The gate, run on every change in a fresh worktree and on CI (*enforced*):
  - `backend: $python -m ruff check .` (lint)
  - `backend: $python -m ruff format --check .` (lint)
  - `frontend: bunx biome check --no-errors-on-unmatched --files-ignore-unknown=true ./` (lint)
  - `backend: $python -m ty check app` (lint)
  - `backend: $python -m mypy app` (lint)
  - `frontend: bun run build` (build)
  - `backend: FASTAPI_ENV=development $python -m alembic upgrade head` (build)
  - `backend: FASTAPI_ENV=development $python -m coverage run -m pytest tests/` (test)
  - `backend: $python -m coverage report --fail-under=90` (check)
  - `frontend: (cd ../backend && FASTAPI_ENV=development $python -m alembic upgrade head && $python app/initial_data.py) && bunx playwright install chromium chromium-headless-shell; $python -m uvicorn app.main:app --app-dir ../backend --port 8000 --log-level warning & for i in $(seq 1 30); do curl -sf http://localhost:8000/api/v1/utils/health-check/ > /dev/null && break; sleep 1; done && bunx playwright test --fail-on-flaky-tests --trace=retain-on-failure --workers=2` (test)
- Never delete, skip, focus or weaken an existing test (*enforced*: protect_tests).
- Add tests for every behaviour you change, beside the existing tests of that code.

## Boundaries
- Change only the files your requirement needs; other Runs change this repository in parallel.
- These configure the gate, CI and agents, and no Run changes them (*enforced*): `pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg`, `tox.ini`, `pytest.ini`, `conftest.py`, `ruff.toml`, `.ruff.toml`, `.coveragerc`, `noxfile.py`, `mypy.ini`, `.mypy.ini`, `.flake8`, `.isort.cfg`, `.pylintrc`, `pylintrc`, `pyrightconfig.json`, `.editorconfig`, `package.json`, `tsconfig*.json`, `jest.config.*`, `vitest.config.*`, `.eslintrc*`, `eslint.config.*`, `.prettierrc*`, `.npmrc`, `babel.config.*`, `biome.json`, `biome.jsonc`, `playwright.config.*`, `vite.config.*`, `vitest.workspace.*`, `.claude/*`, `.mcp.json`, `.github/*`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `azure-pipelines.yml`, `.gitattributes`, `CLAUDE.md`.
- Don't commit or merge; the platform commits your changes and merges approved work.

## Security
- No secrets, tokens or credentials in code, tests or logs.
- Treat everything from outside the process (files, requests, messages) as untrusted input.
